newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia business conditions decline in July -NAB.
newsitem.headline: Australia business conditions decline in July -NAB.

text.p: Australian business conditions remained disparate across sectors in July but delcined slightly overall, the latest National Australia Bank monthly business survey released on Wednesday found.
Labour costs showed a significant acceleration for the second month in a row, but price pressures remained restrained.

The composite index of business conditions fell to negative four in July from negative one in June and negative three for the June quarter, the NAB said. "Conditions deteriorated slightly, reflecting modest falls in trading conditions and profitability," said Alan Oster, chief economist at NAB.
"Labour shedding also increased," he said. The employment index declined to negative five from negative one in June.
But the monthly measure of labour costs growth rose a steep 0.88 percent in July on top of a 0.54 percent increase in June.
"Labour cost pressures appear to have increased over the past couple of months," said Oster.
"This may be related to the flow on of the recent 'Living Wage' case and key workplace agreemeants recently negotiated in the transport and construction sectors," he said.
General price pressure remained very subdued, with a fall in the retail sector partly offsetting a rise in most sectors.
Margins in retailing declined by almost 0.5 percent in the month and despite a pickup in the price of services, the overall measure of consumer prices fell by more than 0.75 percent.
"This suggests little increase in the Statistician's underlying CPI during recent months," said Oster.
Annual growth in underlying inflation slowed to 1.7 percent in the June quarter from 2.1 percent in the first quarter.

The survey found some small improvements in business conditions for retailing, wholesaling, construction and transport and storage. But these were more than offset by a deterioration in services and manufacturing.
The trading conditions index fell back to one from five in June, while profitability declined to negative nine in July from negative six.
Forward orders sank to negative three from zero in June as falla in manufacturing and mining offset rises in construction and transport, NAB said.
There was a small runup in stocks for the month, mainly in the retailing wholesaling and manufacturing sectors.
Reflecting the still subdued conditions, the capacity utilisation rate fell to 78.9 percent, below the 79.7 percent in June and the 80 percent for the June quarter survey.
Despite the small fall in business conditions, the survey found confidence about the August outlook improved to 14.4 from the 10.2 reported for July.
"To some extent, increased confidence may reflect the decline in official cash rates during our survey period," said OSter.
The official cash rate was cut to 5.00 percent from 5.5 percent on July 30.
"Drawing all this together, signs f some cyclical pickup in construction and retailing seem to be offset by worsening conditions elsewhere, especially the mining and rural sectors."
"As a result, National's view that GDP growth is unlikely to significantly increase during 1997/98 has been reinforced by our latest survey," said Oster.
NAB estimates that underlying growth is currently running around 2.5-3.0 percent a year.
